zh: 所以让我们谈谈那部分，如何实际无情地追求人。

speaker: Unknown
en: What are some tactics and stories there of just how you convince these top people to actually talk to you and then join?
zh: 有什么策略和故事，关于你是如何说服这些顶尖的人真正和你交谈然后加入的？

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah.
zh: 是的。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I think one of the things you said a few minutes ago is around, "Hey, this can be a very slow process."
zh: 我认为你几分钟前说的一件事是关于，“嘿，这可能是一个非常缓慢的过程。”

speaker: Unknown
en: And if you're at a zero point, you're at day zero, it can feel like a slow burn.
zh: 如果你处于零点，你在第 0 天，感觉这可能是一种缓慢的燃烧。

speaker: Unknown
en: But imagine over multiple days, you're actually planting all of these seeds with potential top 50 people.
zh: 但想象一下在多天里，你实际上是在所有这些潜在的前 50 人中播种。

speaker: Unknown
en: They're going to come to harvest at different rates, but you got to plant the seeds.
zh: 它们会以不同的速度成熟，但你必须播种。

speaker: Unknown
en: You got to start.
zh: 你必须开始。

speaker: Unknown
en: And because it will take weeks for some, months for others.
zh: 因为对一些人来说需要几周，对另一些人来说需要几个月。

speaker: Unknown
en: I have stories of years of we've worked on candidates, but you have to start the clock on that.
zh: 我有关于我们在候选人身上工作了多少年的故事，但你必须开始那个计时。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so how we think about this relentless pursuit is you'll often reach... one step is just getting them into a conversation, getting a response, getting some kind of engagement.
zh: 所以我们思考这种无情追求的方式是，你通常会到达……一步只是让他们进入对话，得到回复，得到某种参与。

speaker: Unknown
en: But most people will tell you, if you get them, it's like, "Not good timing.
zh: 但大多数人会告诉你，如果你找到了他们，就像，“时机不对。

speaker: Unknown
en: Here's all the reasons I can't do it."
zh: 这是我不能做这件事的所有原因。”

speaker: Unknown
en: And you're like, "Hey, I'm not asking you to interview.
zh: 然后你说，“嘿，我不是在请你面试。

speaker: Unknown
en: I'm not asking you to consider a role.
zh: 我不是在请你考虑一个职位。

speaker: Unknown
en: I'm asking for our next conversation."
zh: 我是在请求我们的下一次对话。”

speaker: Unknown
en: And so when you say, "Hey, it's not really good timing for me right now, maybe in the late fall."
zh: 所以当你说，“嘿，我现在时机真的不太好，也许在深秋。”

speaker: Unknown
en: You're like, "Hey, I totally respect that's great.
zh: 你说，“嘿，我完全尊重，那很棒。

speaker: Unknown
en: But also, you want to come by for a coffee and see the office?
zh: 但还有，你想顺便来喝杯咖啡看看办公室吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: Can I introduce you to this other person on the team who's really fascinated by your work?
zh: 我能把你介绍给团队里这个对你的工作非常着迷的人吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: Can you go chat?"
zh: 你能去聊聊吗？”

speaker: Unknown
en: And so you know it's not... Let's say it's true, they can't join till late fall.
zh: 所以你知道这不是……假设这是真的，他们直到深秋才能加入。

speaker: Unknown
en: That doesn't mean you're not connecting them and having conversations on a weekly basis and working that piece.
zh: 这并不意味着你不连接他们并每周进行对话并处理这件事。

speaker: Unknown
en: And it can only move it forward by doing nothing and actually talking to them in the late fall.
zh: 它只能通过什么都不做并且实际上在深秋与他们交谈来推动它前进。

speaker: Unknown
en: At best you get them, even if they're still interested then or someone else hasn't grabbed them.
zh: 最好的情况是你得到了他们，即使他们那时仍然感兴趣或者其他人没有抓住他们。

speaker: Unknown
en: So we think about this continual touchpoint approach to them, to getting them into process.
zh: 所以我们考虑这种针对他们的持续触点方法，让他们进入流程。

speaker: Unknown
en: But that could... Again, we're willing to do that over days, weeks, months, and sometimes years.
zh: 但这可能……同样，我们愿意在几天、几周、几个月甚至几年内做这件事。

speaker: Unknown
en: When you reach out to someone, imagine working at Cursor now as part of SpaceX, it's like, "Oh, this is interesting and cool."
zh: 当你联系某人时，想象一下现在在 Cursor 作为 SpaceX 的一部分工作，就像，“哦，这很有趣很酷。”

speaker: Unknown
en: And it's like, "Well, you never know, maybe it'll work out someday."
zh: 这就像是，“嗯，你永远不知道，也许有一天它会成功。”

speaker: Unknown
en: A lot of companies... And you've worked with other companies that are not as interesting of a brand and as successful.
zh: 很多公司……你也与其他公司合作过，它们不是那么有趣的品牌，也没有那么成功。

speaker: Unknown
en: Is there any advice for folks to get someone over the line to even talk that works?
zh: 对于那些想要跨过门槛甚至进行有效交谈的人，有什么建议吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: I imagine it's all very particular and nuanced, but just any advice there.
zh: 我想这都非常具体且微妙，但就是那边的任何建议。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah, I think it's really spending a lot of time upfront to get a sense of what could be engaging for them.
zh: 是的，我认为真的要在一开始花大量时间去了解什么对他们来说可能是吸引人的。

speaker: Unknown
en: So who might that be and what might that topic be?
zh: 所以那个人可能是谁，那个话题可能是什么？

speaker: Unknown
en: And so there are a number of excellent people in the world who aren't on any platform.
zh: 所以世界上有很多人很优秀，但他们不在任何平台上。

speaker: Unknown
en: There's no information about them.
zh: 没有关于他们的信息。

speaker: Unknown
en: But most, you can get a couple nuggets.
zh: 但大多数人，你可以得到几个零星的信息。

speaker: Unknown
en: We spend a lot of time here thinking about who can create a warm intro to that person.
zh: 我们在这里花很多时间思考谁能给那个人创造一个热情的介绍。

speaker: Unknown
en: Almost as much effort goes into that than it does the actual messaging.
zh: 几乎和实际发送信息一样多的精力都花在了这上面。

speaker: Unknown
en: Because if you get the right person, that accelerates it.
zh: 因为如果你找对了人，那就会加速这个过程。

speaker: Unknown
en: And once someone's ignored one thing, it's much easier for them to ignore the second and third.
zh: 而且一旦有人忽略了一件事，他们更容易忽略第二和第三件事。

speaker: Unknown
en: But if you get the first one right, you've condensed that activation timeline and effort.
zh: 但如果你把第一件事做对了，你就压缩了那个激活时间线和精力。

speaker: Unknown
en: I've heard that you often say caring is free.
zh: 我听说你经常说关怀是免费的。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah.
zh: 是的。

speaker: Unknown
en: Talk about that because it feels like that connects throughout this entire process.
zh: 聊聊这个吧，因为它感觉就像连接了整个这个过程。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah, I think there's all kind of tactics out there that are of varying degrees of cost, but out-caring other companies, when I've built recruiting teams, that's something that we've always talked about.
zh: 是的，我认为外面有各种各样的策略，成本各不相同，但比其他公司更关怀，当我建立招聘团队时，那是我们一直在谈论的事情。

speaker: Unknown
en: We can care more about that candidate than anyone else.
zh: 我们可以比任何人都更关怀那个候选人。

speaker: Unknown
en: That's in us, that's within us.
zh: 那在我们内心，那是我们内在的能力。

speaker: Unknown
en: We can do that.
zh: 我们能做到。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I think over the history of time, when you look at candidate satisfaction scores, the number one thing that's always there is, "The company generally wanted me.
zh: 我认为纵观历史，当你查看候选人满意度分数时，始终存在的第一件事是，“公司普遍想要我。

speaker: Unknown
en: They made it feel like I belong there."
zh: 他们让我感觉我属于那里。”

speaker: Unknown
en: And so the more that we can care for our candidates and demonstrate that, I think is an unfair advantage and it's in all of us.
zh: 所以我们越是能关怀我们的候选人并展示出来，我认为这是一种不公平的优势，而且它存在于我们所有人心中。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so that is an effort and that is a extra step type of thing.
zh: 所以那是一种努力，那是一种额外步骤之类的事情。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's the extra intentionality that you take that I think in a very somewhat feeling like transactional business, like recruiting, if you're doing this step-by-step funnel of doom, you get caught up in the steps.
zh: 那是你采取的额外的意图性，我认为在一种感觉非常有交易性质的生意中，比如招聘，如果你正在做这种逐步的厄运漏斗，你会陷入这些步骤中。

speaker: Unknown
en: You get caught up in the numbers game.
zh: 你会陷入数字游戏中。

speaker: Unknown
en: "I need to reach out to a hundred to get to 20.
zh: “我需要联系一百个才能得到 20 个。

speaker: Unknown
en: I need to have 10 hire manager screens to get four onsite."
zh: 我需要 10 个招聘经理筛选才能得到 4 个现场面试。”

speaker: Unknown
en: You get caught up in the numbers and you lose the human element.
zh: 你会陷入数字中而失去了人情味。

speaker: Unknown
en: You're looking for the one.
zh: 你在寻找那一个。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's like I tried to remind my team, "We're trying to hire one person for this role here, not 10.
zh: 就像我试着提醒我的团队，“我们试图为这个角色雇佣一个人，而不是 10 个。

speaker: Unknown
en: So don't get caught up in the 10, focus on the one."
zh: 所以不要陷入那 10 个，专注于那一个。”

speaker: Unknown
en: That is such a big reframe in this way of thinking.
zh: 在这种思维方式中，这是一个巨大的重构。

speaker: Unknown
en: As you said, instead of this funnel of we need 200 people at the top to get one at the bottom, you're just like, "Here's the 50 people that would be the best 50 in the world for this.
zh: 正如你所说，不是这种我们需要 200 个人在顶端才能在底端得到一个的漏斗，你就像，“这里是 50 个人，他们将是世界上最好的 50 个人。

speaker: Unknown
en: We just need one of these 50."
zh: 我们只需要这 50 个人中的一个。”

speaker: Unknown
en: It feels a lot more doable.
zh: 感觉更可行。

speaker: Unknown
en: And hopefully we're building relationships with dozens of other of those that could be...
zh: 希望我们正在与其中几十个其他人建立关系，他们可能是……

speaker: Unknown
en: So when you talk about this being slow, we're planting seeds, planting seeds, we're planting seeds.
zh: 所以当你谈论这个过程很慢时，我们正在播种，播种，我们正在播种。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I think the other thing that often happens when you get into this funnel of doom mentality is I think you become overly consistent in your hiring approach.
zh: 我认为当你陷入这种厄运漏斗心态时经常发生的另一件事是，我认为你在招聘方法上变得过度一致。

speaker: Unknown
en: And we are very comfortable with bespoke and ad hoc hiring.
zh: 我们非常习惯定制和临时的招聘。

speaker: Unknown
en: That doesn't mean we don't have similar stages for...
zh: 这并不意味着我们没有类似的阶段用于……

speaker: Unknown
en: But who that next conversation is, what they might focus on, I think we get a little robotic sometimes in recruiting with that.
zh: 但是下一次谈话是谁，他们可能关注什么，我认为我们在招聘中有时会变得有点像机器人。

speaker: Unknown
en: So a lot of companies, as they get into higher volume hiring, they might like, "Hey, we have a pool of these interviewers who can do this type of interview."
zh: 所以很多公司，当它们进入大批量招聘时，它们可能会想，“嘿，我们有一组可以做这种类型的面试的面试官。”

speaker: Unknown
en: And they just let fate decide.
zh: 然后它们就让命运来决定。

speaker: Unknown
en: They let availability decide who has that next conversation.
zh: 它们让有空闲来决定谁进行下一次谈话。

speaker: Unknown
en: But the savvy recruiter or the savvy hiring manager is like, "Ooh, they mentioned this thing.
zh: 但精明的招聘人员或精明的招聘经理会想，“噢，他们提到了这件事。

speaker: Unknown
en: Who on our team has that shared interest in that pool?
zh: 我们团队中谁在那个池子里有那个共同的兴趣？

speaker: Unknown
en: Can we be a little bit more prescriptive?
zh: 我们能不能更具规定性一点？

speaker: Unknown
en: And can we orchestrate a much better candidate experience by taking the extra thoughtful step of who might have a better conversation together?"
zh: 我们能不能通过采取谁可能一起进行更好谈话的额外深思熟虑的步骤，来安排一个更好的候选人体验？”

speaker: Unknown
en: It's so interesting hearing just how important that initial contact is for the rest of the process and how much of this is for future seed planting versus even immediately.
zh: 听到最初接触对后续流程有多重要，以及这有多少是为了未来的播种，甚至是立即见效，真是太有趣了。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah, I feel like we put so much energy to the onsite interview, which I totally get.
zh: 是的，我觉得我们把太多的精力放在了现场面试上，这我完全理解。

speaker: Unknown
en: But honestly, the most important one is that hiring manager first conversation.
zh: 但老实说，最重要的一次是招聘经理的第一次谈话。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so it feels like this 50/50 like, "Hey, half the people you talk to hiring manager should come out."
zh: 所以感觉像是一种 50/50 的比例，比如，“嘿，与招聘经理交谈的人中有一半应该能通过。”

speaker: Unknown
en: And I think we underestimate the importance of it because this is who you're going to work with.
zh: 我认为我们低估了它的重要性，因为这是你将来要一起工作的人。

speaker: Unknown
en: This person's going to make the hiring decisions.
zh: 这个人将做出招聘决定。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so they should be asking the most important questions.
zh: 所以他们应该问最重要的问题。

speaker: Unknown
en: They should be pulling out the most important motivators from that candidate.
zh: 他们应该从候选人那里挖掘出最重要的动力。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I feel like we sometimes maybe, we put it into a 30-minute thing often.
zh: 我觉得有时我们可能把它变成了一个 30 分钟的事情。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's 30 minutes, and it feels so important to the rest of that process.
zh: 只有 30 分钟，但它对流程的其余部分感觉如此重要。

speaker: Unknown
en: Especially if instead of, we just need this funnel and work through a bunch of people.
zh: 特别是如果我们不是只需要这个漏斗并处理一堆人的话。

speaker: Unknown
en: This is one of the 50 in the world that could be the best for this.
zh: 这是世界上 50 个可能最适合这个职位的人之一。

speaker: Unknown
en: You might meet three times.
zh: 你可能会见三次面。

speaker: Unknown
en: You might meet four times as a hiring manager before that person actually is fully in process.
zh: 作为招聘经理，在候选人真正进入完整流程之前，你可能会见四面。

speaker: Unknown
en: The way Brie described this in her piece is that you treat hiring as... the atomic unit of hiring as the person, not the job spec and not the role.
zh: Brie 在她的文章中描述这一点的方式是，你将招聘视为……招聘的原子单位是人，而不是职位描述，也不是角色。

speaker: Unknown
en: Correct.
zh: 没错。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I think that makes it incredibly frustrating, imagine for my team, because you're like, "Oh, what's the..." And you're like, "Well..." It's almost like a decision tree.
zh: 我认为这会让情况变得非常令人沮丧，比如想象一下对我的团队来说，因为你会想，“噢，什么是……”然后你会说，“嗯……”这几乎就像一棵决策树。

speaker: Unknown
en: It could go many different ways based off of this conversation.
zh: 基于这次对话，它可能会走向许多不同的方向。

speaker: Unknown
en: But when you are not caught into the numbers game, it feels a little bit less scary when you're really focused on how do we get that person here versus are they the right person for that job?
zh: 但是当你没有陷入数字游戏时，当你真正专注于如何让这个人来到这里，而不是他们是否是这份工作的合适人选时，感觉就不那么可怕了。

speaker: Unknown
en: And because they're on this list, they're innately very popular and in demand.
zh: 而且因为他们在名单上，他们天生就很受欢迎且需求量很大。

speaker: Unknown
en: Is there anything else that works for getting them excited to talk and interested other than soft, the warm intro, things you've shared?
zh: 除了温和的、温暖的开场白和你分享的东西之外，还有什么能让他们兴奋起来交谈并感兴趣的方法吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah.
zh: 是的。

speaker: Unknown
en: I mean, we've done lots of tactics, I think, to get them involved.
zh: 我的意思是，我想我们已经做了很多策略来让他们参与进来。

speaker: Unknown
en: I mean, one thing I just love is breaking bread.
zh: 我的意思是，有一件事我只是很喜欢，那就是一起吃饭。

speaker: Unknown
en: Having a meal with someone is one of the most human and leveling things that you can do.
zh: 与某人共餐是你能做的最有人情味和平等的事情之一。

speaker: Unknown
en: Sharing a meal across the table is just a disarming act and a joining act that I think is just so important.
zh: 在餐桌旁分享食物只是一种解除戒备和结合的行为，我认为这非常重要。

speaker: Unknown
en: So that could be a coffee, it could be a lunch.
zh: 所以这可以是喝咖啡，也可以是吃午餐。

speaker: Unknown
en: It doesn't need to be super formal, but I just think it is a humanizing activity that I think is really important.
zh: 它不需要非常正式，但我认为这是一种人性化的活动，真的非常重要。

speaker: Unknown
en: So we try to center around food and drink as much as possible.
zh: 所以我们尽可能围绕食物和饮料展开。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think we've done other things I think are very useful, which is if they are one of these 50 people, they might be somewhat famous or well-respected.
zh: 我想我们还做了其他我认为非常有用的事情，如果他们是这 50 个人之一，他们可能有点出名或受人尊敬。

speaker: Unknown
en: They probably have an expertise.
zh: 他们可能拥有专业知识。

speaker: Unknown
en: Having them come in and give a talk to the team, having them come in and do a fun side project.
zh: 让他们进来给团队做一个演讲，让他们进来做一个有趣的副业项目。

speaker: Unknown
en: These people, they love to share and learn and they're curious.
zh: 这些人，他们喜欢分享和学习，而且他们很好奇。

speaker: Unknown
en: But also it demonstrates increased interactivity between the two teams around quality and gives them this realistic preview of being there.
zh: 但同时也展示了围绕质量的团队之间增加的互动，并给他们一个在那里的现实预览。

speaker: Unknown
en: We try to play home games as much as we can, bringing them into the office.
zh: 我们尽可能打主场，把他们带到办公室。

speaker: Unknown
en: But we also understand some of the folks early on might want to go to a neutral site of a coffee shop or something too.
zh: 但我们也理解，有些人早期可能想去中立场所，比如咖啡店或其他地方。

speaker: Unknown
en: But we try to play home games when we can because you have the power of the team.
zh: 但我们在可能的时候尽量打主场，因为你拥有团队的力量。

speaker: Unknown
en: You have the power... And so, one analogy I think about is sometimes when some people are considering university early in their lives, you walk onto a campus and you get that feel in your gut.
zh: 你拥有……所以，我想到了一个类比，就像有些人早年考虑大学时，你走进校园，你在直觉中有那种感觉。

speaker: Unknown
en: And you can't really describe, but it's just like, "Ooh, this feels like home."
zh: 你无法真正描述，但就像是，“噢，这感觉像家一样。”

speaker: Unknown
en: We want people to feel that when they walk into the offices of Cursor and that is a priceless moment.
zh: 我们希望人们走进 Cursor 的办公室时有这种感觉，那是无价的时刻。

speaker: Unknown
en: And by the way, it can be a defining...
zh: 顺便说一句，这可能是一个决定性的……

speaker: Unknown
en: It also could not hit.
zh: 也可能没有产生共鸣。

speaker: Unknown
en: And it's good to suss that out early too.
zh: 而且尽早弄清楚这一点也是好的。

speaker: Unknown
en: But for a lot of people, it does hit and we like that moment.
zh: 但对很多人来说，确实产生了共鸣，我们喜欢那个时刻。

speaker: Unknown
en: This resonates so deeply with early days Airbnb.
zh: 这与早期的 Airbnb 产生了如此深的共鸣。

speaker: Unknown
en: I remember Joe Gebbia had the saying, "Just get them in the elevator."
zh: 我记得 Joe Gebbia 有一句名言，“只要让他们进电梯。”

speaker: Unknown
en: And this is because the office was on the second floor of this building.
zh: 这是因为办公室在这栋楼的二楼。

speaker: Unknown
en: You had to go in this elevator to get in.
zh: 你必须进这个电梯才能进去。

speaker: Unknown
en: And that was the whole strategy, "Just get them in the elevator."
zh: 整个策略就是，“只要让他们进电梯。”

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah.
zh: 是的。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah.
zh: 是的。

speaker: Unknown
en: That was more than half the battle.
zh: 那是战斗的大半。

speaker: Unknown
en: Along these lines of breaking bread in home court, I know this might be one of the reasons you guys have a Cafe Cursor right there near the office, and now it's happening all over the world.
zh: 沿着在主场一起吃饭的思路，我知道这可能是你们在办公室附近开了一家 Cafe Cursor 的原因之一，而且现在这正在全球各地发生。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think Ben leads this work-
zh: 我想 Ben 负责这项工作——

speaker: Adam Ward
en: Yeah.

speaker: Unknown
en: ... but there's all these cafes popping up all over the world.
zh: ...但全世界都冒出了很多这样的咖啡馆。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah, I think it's been an interesting... Obviously, it's very much focused on the product and the user, but he and that team have done a really good job of taking that vibe and putting into a moment.
zh: 是的，我认为这很有趣……显然，这非常关注产品和用户，但他和那个团队做得很好，把那种氛围变成了一个时刻。

speaker: Unknown
en: And if you've been in the Cursor offices, it almost feels like you're in a Hogwarts Library.
zh: 如果你去过 Cursor 办公室，感觉几乎就像你在霍格沃茨图书馆里一样。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's very warm and soft, but cafes bring that energy as well.
zh: 它非常温暖和柔和，但咖啡馆也带来了那种能量。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so we've tried to lift that and drop that in really around the world.
zh: 所以我们尝试将那种氛围提升并真正投放到世界各地。

speaker: Unknown
en: And there's also a lot of chalkboards at the office.
zh: 办公室里还有很多黑板。

speaker: Unknown
en: A lot of chalkboards.
zh: 很多黑板。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's, again, this disarming, warm feel that I think really exudes our Midwest vibes.
zh: 同样，这种让人卸下防备、温暖的感觉，我认为真正流露出了我们的中西部氛围。

speaker: Unknown
en: That is sometimes how I describe Cursor.
zh: 这有时就是我描述 Cursor 的方式。

speaker: Unknown
en: Very hardworking, very ambitious, but at the same time, the work speaks for itself and understated as well.
zh: 非常勤奋，非常有野心，但同时，工作本身就说明了一切，而且也很低调。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so I think a lot of our office helps evoke those vibes too.
zh: 所以我认为我们要的很多办公环境也有助于唤起那些氛围。

speaker: Unknown
en: This episode is brought to you by Mercury.
zh: 本集由 Mercury 赞助播出。

speaker: Unknown
en: Radically different banking, loved by over 300,000 entrepreneurs, and now with Command.
zh: 截然不同的银行业务，受到超过 30 万名创业者的喜爱，现在推出了 Command。

speaker: Unknown
en: I've been a customer of Mercury's for over six years.
zh: 我成为 Mercury 的客户已经超过六年了。

speaker: Unknown
en: I have never once though about leaving.
zh: 我从未想过要离开。

speaker: Unknown
en: Mercury is basically what happens when banking is built by product people, not by bankers.
zh: Mercury 基本上就是当银行业务是由产品人而不是银行家构建时会发生的事情。

speaker: Unknown
en: They make it so easy, dare I say fun, to send invoices, move money around, set up virtual cards for folks on my team.
zh: 他们让发送发票、转移资金、为我团队中的人设置虚拟卡变得如此简单，甚至可以说有趣。

speaker: Unknown
en: Does your bank have an API, a terminal native CLI, or an AI-ready MCP server?
zh: 你的银行有 API、终端原生 CLI 还是 AI 就绪的 MCP 服务器吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: I don't think so.
zh: 我不这么认为。

speaker: Unknown
en: And just recently they launched Command, a conversational interface built directly into Mercury, which acts as your financial operator.
zh: 就在最近他们推出了 Command，一个直接内置于 Mercury 中的对话界面，它充当你的财务运营员。

speaker: Unknown
en: I've been using Command to transfer money around to figure out what categories I've been spending the most money in, analyzing my cash flows.
zh: 我一直在使用 Command 来转移资金，弄清楚我在哪些类别上花的钱最多，分析我的现金流。

speaker: Unknown
en: And just today I used it to find out how much I've made from a specific sponsor over the past year.
zh: 就在今天，我用它来弄清楚过去一年我从某个特定赞助商那里赚了多少钱。

speaker: Unknown
en: I just asked, "How much have I made from X over the past year?"
zh: 我只是问：“过去一年我从 X 那里赚了多少钱？”

speaker: Unknown
en: 10 seconds later, I have an answer.
zh: 10 秒钟后，我就得到了答案。

speaker: Unknown
en: It is so freaking cool.
zh: 这简直酷毙了。

speaker: Unknown
en: Visit mercury.com to learn more and apply online in minutes.
zh: 访问 mercury.com 了解更多信息并在几分钟内在线申请。

speaker: Unknown
en: Mercury is a FinTech company, not an FDIC-insured bank.
zh: Mercury 是一家金融科技公司，不是 FDIC 承保的银行。

speaker: Unknown
en: Banking services provided through Choice Financial Group and Column NA Members FDIC.
zh: 银行服务通过 Choice Financial Group 和 Column NA 提供，成员 FDIC。

speaker: Unknown
en: Okay, so if people have been following along, we're working our way through the funnel.
zh: 好的，如果大家一直在跟进，我们正在沿着漏斗一步步进行。

speaker: Unknown
en: This is my strategy here.
zh: 这是我的策略。

speaker: Unknown
en: So we've talked about how to figure out what you're looking for, figure out who these people are, how to get them talking to you.
zh: 所以我们已经谈到了如何弄清楚你在寻找什么，确定这些人是谁，如何让他们和你交谈。

speaker: Unknown
en: Say you got them in the interview stage.
zh: 假设你已经让他们进入了面试阶段。

speaker: Unknown
en: What are some things you've learned about how to increase your signal on the person and identify if they're a good fit and someone you want to make an offer to?
zh: 关于如何增加关于这个人的信号，并识别他们是否适合以及你是否想向他们发出录用通知，你学到了一些什么？

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah, some of it's a little fundamental, which is research has shown that work samples are the highest predictor of success at a company, but yet most companies are still spending a lot of time doing one-to-one across the table assessments.
zh: 是的，其中一些有点基础，研究表明工作样本是公司在预测成功方面最高的指标，然而大多数公司仍然花大量时间进行一对一的面对面评估。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so I think we are famously known for doing long onsite experiences for some of our roles where they do a project and they get work to side by side.
zh: 所以我认为我们之所以出名，是因为我们要对某些职位进行长时间的现场体验，他们会做一个项目，并并肩工作。

speaker: Unknown
en: So that gives us a very strong signal.
zh: 所以这给了我们非常强的信号。

speaker: Unknown
en: It also gives them the candidate tremendous signal.
zh: 它也给了候选人巨大的信号。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so I think this is where most companies get it wrong on the onsite.
zh: 所以我认为这就是大多数公司在现场面试上搞砸的地方。

speaker: Unknown
en: They're almost always buying.
zh: 他们几乎总是在索取。

speaker: Unknown
en: ... On the onsite, they're almost always buying.
zh: ...在现场面试时，他们几乎总是在索取。

speaker: Unknown
en: This is like we are assessing, we're extracting information.
zh: 就像是我们在评估，我们在提取信息。

speaker: Unknown
en: We're not giving much back to the candidate.
zh: 我们没有回馈给候选人多少东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I'm a big fan of the power of self-selection.
zh: 我是自我选择力量的忠实粉丝。

speaker: Unknown
en: And really good self-selection serves really good inputs and data.
zh: 真正好的自我选择服务于真正好的输入和数据。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so we want that experience with a candidate to feel more two-way than most.
zh: 所以我们希望与候选人的这种体验比大多数情况感觉更加双向。

speaker: Unknown
en: So we really think about crafting that onsite experience through who they might meet.
zh: 所以我们真的考虑通过他们可能会遇到谁来精心设计那个现场体验。

speaker: Unknown
en: We talked about that.
zh: 我们谈到了那个。

speaker: Unknown
en: We really clear handpicking who they might meet for those interviews.
zh: 我们非常清楚地精挑细选他们可能会在那些面试中遇到的人。

speaker: Unknown
en: We do a lot of work sample and project type of work to give us good signal, but we also really curate who's greeting them, who's sitting beside them for lunch.
zh: 我们做很多工作样本和项目类型的工作来给我们良好的信号,但我们也非常策划谁在问候他们,谁在午餐时坐在他们旁边。

speaker: Unknown
en: We always try to put it around a meal, a dinner or lunch or a breakfast.
zh: 我们总是尝试把它安排在一顿饭周围,晚餐或午餐或早餐。

speaker: Unknown
en: And everything is really curated to make that as high quality experience for them and get them the data, but also us getting data from people that we feel like are most going to connect with that person.
zh: 一切都经过精心策划,以便为他们提供高质量的体验并为他们获取数据,同时也让我们从我们觉得最能与那个人建立联系的人那里获取数据。

speaker: Unknown
en: Who runs point on this sort of experience?
zh: 谁负责这种体验?

speaker: Unknown
en: Is it a recruiter or is it the hiring manager?
zh: 是招聘人员还是招聘经理?

speaker: Unknown
en: I would say I think it's the recruiter primarily as the quarterback, but they're pulling lots of levers.
zh: 我想我说主要是招聘人员作为四分卫,但他们在拉动很多杠杆。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so the hiring manager is probably going to have the most insight into some of those people.
zh: 所以招聘经理可能对其中一些人有最深入的了解。

speaker: Unknown
en: Our recruiting coordinators are tremendous and I think we probably, and they do a lot of this hosting with us as well.
zh: 我们的招聘协调员非常出色,我想我们可能,他们也和我们一起做很多这种接待工作。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so our recruiting course of course do some scheduling, but they're probably doing more of this candidate shepherding.
zh: 所以我们的招聘课程当然会做一些日程安排,但他们可能更多地在做这种候选人引导工作。

speaker: Unknown
en: So imagine a candidate who's with us for a day or two.
zh: 所以想象一下一位候选人跟我们待了一两天。

speaker: Unknown
en: There's lots of moving pieces and helping them move from a workstation where they might be doing a project into lunch back to that, helping them get their environment set up.
zh: 有很多移动的部分,帮助他们从他们可能正在做项目的工作站移动到午餐再回到那个,帮助他们让他们的环境设置好。

speaker: Unknown
en: So there's a lot of people in play.
zh: 所以有很多人在参与。

speaker: Unknown
en: We ask our recruiter to be the quarterback, but a lot of the insight is coming from hiring managers and execution with the coordinator too.
zh: 我们要求我们的招聘人员做四分卫,但很多见解来自招聘经理,以及与协调员的执行。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's interesting just how much of the experience and process changes with this worldview of every person we are talking to is very special and they're very rare and these are the best for this role.
zh: 有趣的是,有多少体验和流程随着这种世界观而改变,即我们交谈的每个人都是非常特别的,他们是非常罕见的,这些是这个职位的最佳人选。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so it's clear how much of it trickles down into thinking deeply about every touchpoint along the journey versus the typical journey.
zh: 所以很明显,其中有多少渗透到了深入思考旅程中的每一个接触点,而不是典型的旅程。

speaker: Adam Ward
en: And imagine that you have teams and employee base who understand that well, they went through it. So you get over this tipping point moment with a company where they had that experience. So they recognize, acknowledge it. Now they're part of how fun is that? They had a great experience. Now they get to help deliver that for this next batch of people.
zh: 想象一下你有团队和员工基础,他们理解这一点,他们经历过它。所以你克服了公司的这个临界点时刻,他们有了那个体验。所以他们认可,承认它。现在他们成为了其中的一部分,那多有趣?他们有了很棒的体验。现在他们得以帮助为下一批人提供这种体验。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's recursive.
zh: 这是递归的。

speaker: Unknown
en: So you kind of create this flywheel opportunity once you get over that initial hump.
zh: 所以一旦你克服了最初的障碍,你就会创造出这种飞轮机会。

speaker: Unknown
en: I just remembered actually, I had a friend applying for a job at Cursor and he said it was the best candidate experience he's ever had.
zh: 我其实刚刚想起来,我有一个朋友申请 Cursor 的工作,他说这是他拥有的最好的候选人体验。

speaker: Unknown
en: Just remember that.
zh: 就记住那个。

speaker: Unknown
en: So by definition, we though about doing a lot of scoping of really great people.
zh: 所以根据定义,我们考虑做很多范围界定非常优秀的人。

speaker: Unknown
en: Not all of them are going to be a fit for us by their choice or ours, but every one of them can walk away as a net promoter.
zh: 不是所有人都适合我们,由他们的选择或我们的选择,但每个人都可以作为一个净推荐者离开。

speaker: Unknown
en: And again, by definition, they're some of the best.
zh: 同样,根据定义,他们中的一些是最好的。

speaker: Unknown
en: Those promoters weigh more and count more than others because they're influential, they're great, they're known to be good.
zh: 这些推荐者的分量更重,计数更多,因为他们有影响力,他们很棒,他们被认为是好的。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so they may never come back to us, but they might tell you who now tells this audience or they might tell you who then you mentioned something at a barbecue and now it becomes this ground swell and you start to build a little stronger magnet.
zh: 所以他们可能永远不会回到我们这里,但他们可能会告诉你谁现在告诉这个受众,或者他们可能会告诉你谁,然后你在烧烤会上提到一些事情,现在它变成了这种 ground swell,你开始建立一个更强的磁铁。

speaker: Unknown
en: And that activation becomes a little bit less hard if you do that well.
zh: 如果你做得好,这种激活就会变得不那么困难。

speaker: Unknown
en: Absolutely.
zh: 绝对的。

speaker: Unknown
en: The work trial piece, I saw an interview with Michael Terrell talking about this, and he said how they tried to get rid of it because it obviously adds a lot of load and some people don't want to be doing these things.
zh: 工作试用部分,我看到 Michael Terrell 谈到这个的采访,他说他们如何试图摆脱它,因为它显然增加了很多负担,有些人不想做这些事情。

speaker: Unknown
en: And he said that it just totally tanked their signal and they had to bring it back.
zh: 他说这完全毁了他们的信号,他们不得不把它带回来。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah, it's a huge commitment you can imagine of time.
zh: 是的,你可以想象这是一个巨大的时间承诺。

speaker: Unknown
en: But if talent is your number one thing, then that is a good investment of time to do it.
zh: 但如果人才是你的第一要务,那么这是时间的良好投资。

speaker: Unknown
en: We all have a role to play in recruiting at the company.
zh: 我们在公司招聘中都有角色要扮演。

speaker: Unknown
en: Not everyone is carved out or best to do trial work, but some are.
zh: 不是每个人都适合或最适合做试用工作,但有些人是。

speaker: Unknown
en: But some can do the lunch, some could do the greet.
zh: 但有些人可以做午餐,有些人可以做问候。

speaker: Unknown
en: So there's lots of different ways that people can play a role.
zh: 所以人们有很多不同的方式可以扮演角色。

speaker: Unknown
en: But yeah, when we ran that experiment, because it is quite expensive, it is also a big ask of candidates.
zh: 但是是的,当我们运行那个实验时,因为它相当昂贵,它也是对候选人的一个大要求。

speaker: Unknown
en: We really struggled to have confidence in our decision.
zh: 我们真的很难对我们的决定有信心。

speaker: Unknown
en: Again, this is a confidence building function, and so we are excited to bring it back.
zh: 同样,这是一个建立信心的功能,所以我们很兴奋把它带回来。

speaker: Unknown
en: So a good learning there is it's like if you are not doing this, you are lacking significant signal.
zh: 所以那里一个很好的学习是,就像如果你不这样做,你就缺乏重要的信号。

speaker: Unknown
en: Possibly.
zh: 可能的。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah, I think so.
zh: 是的,我是这么认为。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I don't think there's a lot of maxims or absolutes in this business, but I think for a lot of companies, it's hard to think of a better way than doing side-by-side real work to get those signals.
zh: 我不认为在这个业务中有很多格言或绝对的东西,但我认为对于很多公司来说,很难想到比并肩做现实工作更好的方法来获得那些信号。

speaker: Unknown
en: Obviously some of it in this case is a technical signal, but imagine the amount of core values and collaboration and other signals you get over a stretch of time that could be arguably more important than the specific technical skill.
zh: 显然在这种情况下其中一些是技术信号,但想象一下在一段时间内你获得的核心价值观和协作以及其他信号的数量,这些可以说可能比特定的技术技能更重要。

speaker: Unknown
en: What do you do for PMs or, I don't know, go-to-market or ops people?
zh: 你们为 PM 或我不知道, go-to-market 或运营人员做什么?

speaker: Unknown
en: Is there something like that?
zh: 有类似的东西吗?

speaker: Unknown
en: We have a version of this across.
zh: 我们在这方面有一个版本。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so the go-to-market team does a challenge where they work through a challenge together, a challenging customer, things like that.
zh: 所以 go-to-market 团队做一个挑战,他们一起解决一个挑战,一个棘手的客户,诸如此类。

speaker: Unknown
en: And that's often one-to-one with a hiring manager.
zh: 而这通常与招聘经理是一对一的。

speaker: Unknown
en: Product does a similar project type together as well.
zh: 产品部门也会一起做类似类型的项目。

speaker: Unknown
en: So we have versions of that that I feel like are titrated to the function, but also the role and things like that as well.
zh: 所以我们有针对不同职能调整的这种版本，但我感觉也是针对角色以及诸如此类因素调整的。

speaker: Unknown
en: So we try not to be uniform across this because these functions are very different.
zh: 所以我们试图不在此上保持一致，因为这些职能是非常不同的。

speaker: Unknown
en: One of the classic criticisms with the work trial is you're doing work for the company and it's like, "Oh, we're just solving problems for you for free."
zh: 对工作试用经典的批评之一是你在为公司工作，这就像是，“噢，我们只是在为你免费解决问题。”

speaker: Unknown
en: What's the philosophy on the problem they tackle, say engineering or PM?
zh: 对于他们解决的问题，比如工程或 PM，有什么哲学看法？

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah, there's a set of problems they can choose from.
zh: 是的，有一组问题可供他们选择。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so they feel like they have some direction and discretion.
zh: 所以他们感觉他们有一些方向和裁量权。

speaker: Unknown
en: We also are very open to right sizing it for them based on where they are and their availability and time too, up to a certain extent.
zh: 在一定程度上，我们也非常愿意根据他们的情况、他们的可用性和时间来为他们调整规模。

speaker: Unknown
en: So we try to be flexible and understanding around that.
zh: 所以我们努力对此保持灵活和理解。

speaker: Unknown
en: And we also will sometimes use Saturdays too.
zh: 我们有时也会利用星期六。

speaker: Unknown
en: So we understand it can be hard to take time away on a work week or a traditional work week.
zh: 所以我们明白在工作周或传统工作周中抽出时间可能很难。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so we totally get it.
zh: 所以我们完全理解。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's a big ask, a big commitment.
zh: 这是一个很大的要求，一个很大的承诺。

speaker: Unknown
en: We think it's worth it, but we're also willing to schedule that when that works for them.
zh: 我们认为这是值得的，但我们也愿意在他们方便的时候安排。

speaker: Unknown
en: So there's this conflict around a lot of time and effort that could feel slow, but when they're ready to go, we are fast.
zh: 所以这里存在一种冲突，涉及大量可能感觉缓慢的时间和精力，但当他们准备好出发时，我们是快的。

speaker: Unknown
en: We make up that time.
zh: 我们弥补那个时间。

speaker: Unknown
en: So if you and I were having an initial screen, you're like, "Yeah, okay, I'll be open to talking to hiring manager."
zh: 所以如果你和我正在进行初步筛选，你会说，“是的，好的，我愿意和招聘经理谈谈。”

speaker: Unknown
en: Open up your calendar.
zh: 打开你的日历。

speaker: Unknown
en: I have their calendar.
zh: 我有他们的日历。

speaker: Unknown
en: Great.
zh: 太好了。

speaker: Unknown
en: You're going to talk to them in an hour.
zh: 你将在一小时内与他们交谈。

speaker: Unknown
en: So once they're ready to go, you got to capitalize on that.
zh: 所以一旦他们准备好出发，你必须利用那个机会。

speaker: Unknown
en: You can't create openings for them to have second guessing.
zh: 你不能为他们创造犹豫的机会。

speaker: Unknown
en: So when we go, we go, but it might take a lot of time to get up to that moment.
zh: 所以当我们行动时，我们就行动，但达到那个时刻可能需要很多时间。

speaker: Unknown
en: Moving ourselves further down the funnel, what's the moment when you decide we're going to make this person an offer?
zh: 让我们进一步深入漏斗，决定我们要向这个人发出 offer 的时刻是什么时候？

speaker: Unknown
en: Is there something that you look for specifically and/or just what's the process like a hiring committee meeting is something else?
zh: 有什么你特别寻找的东西，或者只是像招聘委员会会议那样的流程是怎样的？

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah, we debrief as immediately as possible as a team.
zh: 是的，我们作为一个团队尽可能快地做汇报。

speaker: Unknown
en: Each function has a little bit of a different hiring process of what that looks like, but we don't have hiring committees.
zh: 每个职能的招聘流程看起来有点不同，但我们没有招聘委员会。

speaker: Unknown
en: It is hiring manager led.
zh: 它是由招聘经理主导的。

speaker: Unknown
en: They get lots of input from the team.
zh: 他们从团队那里获得大量意见。

speaker: Unknown
en: And remember the role of the hiring manager is, it's not a democracy.
zh: 并且要记住招聘经理的角色是，这不是民主。

speaker: Unknown
en: Hiring manager is holding that group accountable for helping them get them the right inputs to make out the right decision, to make the best decision, hire or no hire.
zh: 招聘经理要让那个团队对帮助他们获得正确的输入以做出正确的决策、做出最佳决策、录用或不录用负责。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so we try to frame it in that way, making sure we get really good signal on it.
zh: 所以我们试图以此方式构建它，确保我们获得关于它的真正好的信号。

speaker: Unknown
en: So we try to move really quickly.
zh: 所以我们试图非常快地行动。

speaker: Unknown
en: So debriefing's typically same day, if not next day.
zh: 所以汇报通常在同一天，如果不是的话就是第二天。

speaker: Unknown
en: And they make that decision, then that decision goes to the founders for stamping.
zh: 然后他们做出决定，那个决定就会交给创始人进行批准。

speaker: Unknown
en: Awesome.
zh: 太棒了。

speaker: Unknown
en: Okay.
zh: 好的。

speaker: Unknown
en: Then you get to the offer stage.
zh: 然后你到了 offer 阶段。

speaker: Unknown
en: There's a bunch of stuff here, but one is just there are many massive offers happening these days.
zh: 这里有很多东西，但其中之一只是现在有很多大规模的 offer 发生。

speaker: Unknown
en: Okay, so say you made an offer to one of these top 50 people and they're like, "Okay, but I also got this offer from Anthropic for a bazillion dollars."
zh: 好的，假设你向这前 50 人中的一个发出了 offer，他们说，“好的，但我也收到了 Anthropic 的价值天文数字的 offer。”

speaker: Unknown
en: How do you handle that?
zh: 你如何处理那个？

speaker: Unknown
en: And also just, is that super frustrating or is it like, "Oh wow, more signal, this person is incredible."
zh: 还有只是，那是超级令人沮丧的，还是像，“噢哇，更多信号，这人是不可思议的。”

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah, I think it can be both.
zh: 是的，我认为两者皆有可能。

speaker: Unknown
en: There's room for both.
zh: 两者都有空间。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think that the goal is to not be selling at the close.
zh: 我认为目标不是在最后关头推销。

speaker: Unknown
en: We're trying to sell throughout.
zh: 我们试图在整个过程中推销。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so if you think about the craft of recruiting, the craft of recruiting is upfront getting a really clear on this person's motivations and why they might make a move and for what.
zh: 所以如果你思考招聘的艺术，招聘的艺术是提前非常清楚地了解这个人的动机以及他们可能为什么以及为了什么而变动。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then making sure that that entire experience hits to those pieces.
zh: 然后确保整个体验都能触及到这些点。

speaker: Unknown
en: So at the end is a culmination, not a start.
zh: 所以在最后是一个顶点，而不是一个开始。

speaker: Unknown
en: It feels almost like a natural outcome of it where just like, "Oh, this is almost like this assumptive next step of, yeah, and here's the offer that we talked about all along."
zh: 这感觉几乎就像一个自然的结果，就像，“哦，这几乎就像这个假设性的下一步，是的，这就是我们一直谈论的那个提议。”

speaker: Unknown
en: Versus starting the clock or starting the conversation on a close.
zh: 而不是开始计时或开始关于结束的对话。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think we try to get back to those motivations.
zh: 我认为我们试图回到那些动机。

speaker: Unknown
en: So we might think about how we would differentiate against Anthropic size wise or the role or the team or the people you work with.
zh: 所以我们要考虑如何在规模、角色、团队或与你共处的人方面与 Anthropic 区分开来。

speaker: Unknown
en: We really try to focus on the intrinsic things, not the extrinsic things, which is very hard to do when you're getting MBA players offers and salaries and sometimes bigger than that.
zh: 我们真的试图关注内在的事物，而不是外在的事物，当你在给 MBA 球员提供报价和薪水，有时甚至比那更多时，这很难做到。

speaker: Unknown
en: But we really try to focus on people who want to be here.
zh: 但我们真的试图关注那些想要在这里的人。

speaker: Unknown
en: And often when people are thinking about their job search and what might be next, they maybe start with a set of things and we maybe help them discover other things along the way.
zh: 而且通常当人们在考虑他们的求职和下一步可能是什么时，他们可能从一组事情开始，我们也许帮助他们在此过程中发现其他事情。

speaker: Unknown
en: And we might discover at the end that actually, this is not the right fit and that's okay.
zh: 我们可能会在最后发现实际上这并不是合适的匹配，那也没关系。

speaker: Unknown
en: And we feel good about walking away from that.
zh: 我们对离开那个感觉良好。

speaker: Unknown
en: But often it's around helping them discover that actually maybe this is the right place through that journey.
zh: 但通常是在帮助他们发现实际上也许通过那个旅程这里是合适的地方。

speaker: Unknown
en: How often do people take a job that doesn't have the highest comp?
zh: 多久人们会接受一份没有最高薪酬的工作？

speaker: Unknown
en: Is that common or is that rare?
zh: 这是常见的还是罕见的？

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah, I think you're trying to mitigate comp as a reason people come or don't come.
zh: 是的，我认为你试图减轻薪酬作为人们来或不来的一个理由。

speaker: Unknown
en: And often that means it's not the highest number.
zh: 而且通常那意味着它不是最高的数字。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I think we've all probably talked with people who maybe at some point in their career chase just the largest number.
zh: 我想我们大家都可能和那些在职业生涯的某个阶段只追逐最大数字的人谈过。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I think what you realize six months in is that just becomes your new level of comp life, but you're not excited by the people you work with or the work you're doing.
zh: 而我认为你会在六个月后意识到，这只是成为了你新的薪酬生活水准，但你对你一起工作的人或你做的工作并不感到兴奋。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so we try to mitigate that as a piece, but I think it happens a lot.
zh: 所以我们试图减轻那作为一部分，但我认为这发生了很多。

speaker: Unknown
en: And also rightfully so, we've probably lost people where maybe we were the highest one and they went somewhere else too.
zh: 而且也是理所当然的，我们可能失去了一些人，也许我们要的是最高的，他们去了别的地方。

speaker: Unknown
en: And if that's the right fit for them, this is going to sound a little polyannic, but I fundamentally believe there are right people for right companies at the right time.
zh: 如果那是他们的合适匹配，这听起来可能有点天真，但我根本相信在正确的时间有正确的人对应正确的公司。

speaker: Unknown
en: And if they discover at the end of that that we're not, that's the right call for them.
zh: 如果他们在最后发现我们不是，那对他们来说是正确的选择。

speaker: Unknown
en: And as a recruiter, if they're not the right fit, I literally have to redo that work in six months.
zh: 作为招聘人员，如果他们不是合适的匹配，我真的必须在六个月重做那个工作。

speaker: Unknown
en: I don't want to redo that work.
zh: 我不想重做那个工作。

speaker: Unknown
en: I'd rather let's figure that out right now and have that more open conversation.
zh: 我宁愿我们现在就弄清楚并拥有那个更开放的对话。

speaker: Unknown
en: You should build an agent that helps you decide and figure that out, which company is the right fit for me right now in this time because that sounds really valuable to check that price.
zh: 你应该建立一个智能体来帮助你决定并弄清楚那个，哪家公司现在这个时候是我的合适匹配，因为检查那个价格听起来真的很有价值。

speaker: Unknown
en: That'd be super interesting.
zh: 那会超级有趣。

speaker: Unknown
en: Something that I've heard Anthropic does that I've never heard anyone do, similar to Tesla, they don't let you negotiate.
zh: 我听说 Anthropic 做的一件事我从没听说过别人做的，类似于特斯拉，他们不让你谈判。

speaker: Unknown
en: They're just like, "Here's the offer."
zh: 他们就像，“这是提议。”

speaker: Unknown
en: Do you feel like that's an only Anthropic thing that they could do because they're just Anthropic?
zh: 你觉得那是 Anthropic 因为是 Anthropic 才能做的事吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: Or is that something you think about?
zh: 还是那是你考虑的事情？

speaker: Unknown
en: I mean, I've thought about it.
zh: 我的意思是，我考虑过。

speaker: Unknown
en: I see over time different companies have done that.
zh: 我看到随着时间的推移不同的公司做过那个。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I think what I respect about it is you make that call and you kind of stick with it and there's a commitment to it.
zh: 我想我对此尊重的是你做出那个决定并且你有点坚持它并且有一个承诺。

speaker: Unknown
en: But every company's different and I think the approach is...
zh: 但每个公司是不同的，我认为方法是……

speaker: Unknown
en: So I respect it.
zh: 所以我尊重它。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think about it, but it may not be right for us.
zh: 我考虑它，但它可能不适合我们。

speaker: Unknown
en: From the candidate's perspective, what are some mistakes that people make when they get an offer that shoot themselves in the foot?
zh: 从候选人的角度看，人们得到提议时犯了哪些错误让自己搬起石头砸自己的脚？

speaker: Unknown
en: Generally, the advice I give to candidates is when you think about your offer and if you're negotiating, it has to just fit a line of logic.
zh: 通常，我给候选人的建议是当你考虑你的提议并且如果你在谈判，它必须符合逻辑线。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so if you are asking for a certain piece of compensation or a certain other piece of it, is it rooted?
zh: 所以如果你要求某一部分薪酬或它的某个其他部分，它是根植的吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: Walk me through the logic behind it.
zh: 向我解释它背后的逻辑。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think that makes it easy for the person to understand, but also easy for them to communicate that forward to maybe a different decision maker as well.
zh: 我认为这让那个人容易理解，但也让他们容易将其传达给也许不同的决策者。

speaker: Unknown
en: So I see candidates who are maybe a little bit all over the place on that, where early on it's this and now it's this and it's kind of the add-on type of thing versus a candid who's coming in of here's the four things that are important to me and being clear and consistent with it as much from the outset as you can.
zh: 所以我看到候选人在那个上面可能有点到处都是，早期是这个现在是这是那种附加类型的东西对比进来的候选人是这四个是对我重要的并且从开始尽可能清晰和一致。

speaker: Unknown
en: Not all things can be there at the outset.
zh: 并非所有事情可以在开始就在那里。

speaker: Unknown
en: That makes it very logical and easy for the company to engage with that.
zh: 这使它非常合乎逻辑并且容易让公司参与其中。

speaker: Unknown
en: Versus just finding random excuses for more comp.
zh: 而不是只是为更多薪酬找随机的借口。

speaker: Unknown
en: Correct.
zh: 正确。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I think what a company generally knows is we're intrinsically not their top choice.
zh: 我认为公司通常知道的是我们本质上不是他们的首选。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so we're trying to win head and hearts here and we're not trying to buy that out.
zh: 所以我们要在这里赢得头脑和心灵，我们不是试图买那个。

speaker: Unknown
en: How just mind-blowing are these comps these days?
zh: 这些天这些薪酬是多么令人难以置信？

speaker: Unknown
en: I imagine you've seen so many.
zh: 我想你见过这么多。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah, I think it's all true and worse or higher.
zh: 是的，我认为这都是真的，而且情况甚至更糟或更高。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think the open question, a lot of us AI companies are like, "How does it go from here?
zh: 我认为这是一个悬而未决的问题，很多我们这些 AI 公司都在想，「从这里开始会怎么走？

speaker: Unknown
en: How does this end?"
zh: 这会如何结束？」

speaker: Unknown
en: Nobody knows.
zh: 没人知道。

speaker: Unknown
en: But it does feel like the unit of measure that matters the most is the most fixed and finite, which is time.
zh: 但确实感觉最重要的衡量单位是最固定且有限的，那就是时间。

speaker: Unknown
en: It is a race against the clock to get the model, the talent.
zh: 这是一场与时间赛跑的比赛，为了获得模型、人才。

speaker: Unknown
en: And that is the thing that matters the most is the most precious.
zh: 而且最重要的是那件事，也是最宝贵的。

speaker: Unknown
en: Clearly for some companies, there's more money and there's more other things, but time is the most fixed and important asset right here in this market.
zh: 显然对于一些公司来说，有更多的钱和其他东西，但在当前这个市场上，时间是最固定且重要的资产。

speaker: Unknown
en: Just coming back to the AI researcher trend, it's crazy how these people used to be just off on the side building these AI models, ML models, not that exciting to anybody, and now they're the most in demand.
zh: 回到 AI 研究人员的趋势，这些人过去只是在一边构建这些 AI 模型、ML 模型，对任何人来说都没那么令人兴奋，现在却如此抢手，这真是太疯狂了。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I remember I helped build out the research group at Facebook before... they'd just not hire PhDs, even advanced degrees really much at all.
zh: 我记得我曾在……之前帮助 Facebook 建立研究团队，他们甚至不招聘博士，甚至也不怎么招聘拥有高级学位的人。

speaker: Unknown
en: And this is 2010 or something.
zh: 那是 2010 年左右。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I remember meeting just this set of academics really who were getting this growing frustration of their work, not ever making it outside of the halls of academia.
zh: 我记得遇到了一群这样的学者，他们对他们的工作感到越来越沮丧，因为他们的工作从未走出过学术殿堂。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so I'm very excited for that population to have this moment.
zh: 所以我对这个群体能拥有这一刻感到非常兴奋。

speaker: Unknown
en: They've been arguably the underpinning of technical innovation for decades and they're having their moment and well-deserved.
zh: 可以说，几十年来他们一直是技术创新的基石，现在他们迎来了他们的时刻，这是实至名归的。

speaker: Unknown
en: Kind of along those lines to close out the funnel of, let's call it the funnel of joy instead of the funnel of doom.
zh: 沿着这些线索，为了让我们称之为「快乐漏斗」而不是「厄运漏斗」的漏斗收尾。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah, love it.
zh: 是的，我很喜欢。

speaker: Unknown
en: I heard from one of your candidates, here's the quote that I got, that you and your team's ability to close and convert candidates with offers to accept is extraordinary.
zh: 我听你的一个候选人说过，我引用一下我得到的话，你和你的团队让候选人接受 offer 并入职的能力是非凡的。

speaker: Unknown
en: What are some things you do that help get someone over the line that are kind of on the fence?
zh: 你们采取了哪些措施来帮助那些犹豫不决的人下定决心？

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah.
zh: 是的。

speaker: Unknown
en: So I think there's a couple things there.
zh: 所以我认为有几件事。

speaker: Unknown
en: One, I'll just re-mention quickly, which is that the closing is happening throughout the process in terms of who they're meeting and motivations and removing objections along the way.
zh: 第一，我就简单重申一下，那就是整个流程中都在进行成交，关于他们见谁、动机如何，以及沿途消除异议。

speaker: Unknown
en: So that's one.
zh: 这是第一点。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think the second is closing is a team sport.
zh: 我认为第二点是成交是一项团队运动。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so when we have a candidate, particularly a high profile, high caliber, there are often daily standups around that candidate about what we're doing to get them to yes.
zh: 所以当我们有一个候选人，特别是高知名度、高素质的，通常会有关于该候选人的每日站会，讨论我们在做什么让他们点头。

speaker: Unknown
en: And that might be 10 minutes, but it's not the amount of time.
zh: 可能只有 10 分钟，但时间长短不是重点。

speaker: Unknown
en: It is a focused energy every day around what we are collectively doing.
zh: 这是每天集中的精力，关注我们在集体做什么。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so that could be the hiring manager recruiter, but also could be former peers.
zh: 所以这可能包括招聘经理、招聘人员，但也可能是前同事。

speaker: Unknown
en: There's lots of people who influence that, and we try to just be very intentional about making sure that person feels cared for and coming here and staying on top of things.
zh: 有很多人对此有影响力，我们试图非常有意识地确保那个人感到被关心，来这里，并紧跟事态。

speaker: Unknown
en: The third thing I think is we just try to make it very personal.
zh: 我认为第三件事是我们只是试图让它非常个性化。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so just this week, two days ago, I just saw, and we try to share these stories internally too, because this is how it builds the culture of recruiting.
zh: 就在本周，两天前，我刚看到，我们也试图在内部分享这些故事，因为这就是建立招聘文化的方式。

speaker: Unknown
en: We kind of share these stories back to the company.
zh: 我们将这些故事分享回公司。

speaker: Unknown
en: But someone was sharing, we were working on a candidate in New York and we learned that through getting to know them that they went to a performing arts high school and were a classically trained violinist and was just very into stringed instruments.
zh: 有人分享说，我们在纽约处理一个候选人，通过了解他们，我们知道他们去了表演艺术高中，是受过古典训练的小提琴手，并且非常痴迷于弦乐器。

speaker: Unknown
en: So this person found this specialty store in New York City and bought this kind of unique Turkish guitar, almost violin guitar thing.
zh: 所以这个人在纽约市找到了这家特色店，买了这个独特的土耳其吉他，几乎是那种小提琴吉他之类的东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: And they're meeting for a dinner where they got the offer and he presented that gift to them.
zh: 他们在一次晚餐中见面，那时他们拿到了 offer，他把那个礼物送给了他们。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so it was a couple hundred dollars maybe.
zh: 所以可能花了几百美元。

speaker: Unknown
en: Not a lot of money, particularly relative to the size of offer and the size of impact that we thought that someone's going to have.
zh: 没多少钱，特别是相对于 offer 的规模和我们认为这个人将产生的影响力规模而言。

speaker: Unknown
en: But it's the thoughtfulness and the touch and the uniqueness of it and the personal moment of that that I think stands out.
zh: 但这是其中的体贴、接触、独特性，以及我认为突出的个人时刻。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I think when a candidate thinks about having the best candidate experience, often they feel like, "Wow, this felt tailored to me.
zh: 我认为当候选人考虑到拥有最好的候选人体验时，他们经常觉得，「哇，这感觉是为我量身定做的。

speaker: Unknown
en: This felt unique to me."
zh: 这感觉对我来说是独一无二的。」

speaker: Unknown
en: I know there's also a Slack channel that gets created for each candidate.
zh: 我知道每个候选人都会创建一个 Slack 频道。

speaker: Unknown
en: Can we discuss this for a second?
zh: 我们能稍微讨论一下这个吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: Every candidate.
zh: 每个候选人。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah.
zh: 是的。

speaker: Unknown
en: So I think when you talk about the standup, sometimes that's also strategy and updates.
zh: 所以我认为当你谈到站会时，有时那也是策略和更新。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so there's the same rallying effect to activate is no different at that close.
zh: 所以那种激活的集结效应在成交阶段没有什么不同。

speaker: Unknown
en: And each candidate has their own channel.
zh: 每个候选人都有自己的频道。

speaker: Unknown
en: So much of this just keeps coming back to intentionality around every specific candidate and not treating it like the funnel, but just this is the atomic unit, this person, what can we do throughout the entire process to make them get excited and see if it's a fit?
zh: 很多事情都回到了对每个特定候选人的意图性，而不是把它当作漏斗，而是这个人这个原子单位，我们在整个过程中能做什么来让他们兴奋并看看是否合适？

speaker: Unknown
en: Which is hard to do when you're doing at scale at the funnel of doom.
zh: 当你在「厄运漏斗」中大规模操作时，这很难做到。

speaker: Unknown
en: So when you are thinking about a hundred candidates for every role, then that does not scale.
zh: 所以当你考虑到每个职位有一百个候选人时，那是无法扩展的。

speaker: Unknown
en: But when you're narrowing that down to a small percentage of people that you've been laying groundwork with over time, because now people are moving faster through those steps and it's a smaller number of people.

en: We'd seen all these companies over time and worked with labs and all these things.

speaker: Unknown
en: We're like, "Wow, these companies are literally at the cutting edge of a technical revolution here."
zh: 我们想，「哇，这些公司实际上处于技术革命的最前沿。」

en: Probably the most exciting one we've seen in millennia.
zh: 可能是我们在几千年中见过的最激动人心的一次。

speaker: Unknown
en: And they are recruiting in a web browser way.
zh: 而他们正在以一种 Web 浏览器的方式招聘。

speaker: Unknown
en: And we're like, "If a company had this willingness to commit this time and effort as this collective force, they could really have an unfair advantage when it comes to talent."
zh: 我们想，「如果一家公司有意愿投入这种时间和精力作为这种集体力量，他们在人才方面实际上可以拥有不公平的优势。」

speaker: Unknown
en: And when you think about companies over time, whether they become this iconic logo or one that we no longer recognize, it often isn't the first company, the fastest to market, the first idea.
zh: 当你随时间考虑这些公司时，无论它们成为这个标志性的 Logo 还是我们不再认识的一个，通常往往不是第一家上市的公司，不是第一个想法。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's actually execution.
zh: 实际上是执行。

speaker: Unknown
en: And execution comes down to having the right talent at the right time.
zh: 而执行归结为在正确的时间拥有正确的人才。

speaker: Unknown
en: And when companies figure that out, they're like, "Ooh, this is the most important thing and this is how we're going to approach it."
zh: 当公司弄明白这一点时，他们会想，「哦，这是最重要的事情，这就是我们要解决它的方法。」

speaker: Unknown
en: And so when we met Cursor, we're like, "This could be fun."
zh: 所以当我们遇到 Cursor 时，我们想，「这可能会很有趣。」

speaker: Unknown
en: Cursor is actually such a great example of exactly what you're describing because it feels like throughout the entire history of Cursor, it was always just like, how are they going to survive?
zh: Cursor 实际上是一个非常好的例子，完全符合你所描述的，因为在 Cursor 的整个历史中，感觉就像，他们将如何生存？

speaker: Unknown
en: There's these model companies building these things, the IDs.
zh: 有这些模型公司在构建这些东西，IDEs。

speaker: Unknown
en: People are moving away from IDs.

speaker: Unknown
en: And it's been incredible to watch Cursor execute and get ahead of each of these shifts whenever people doubt that there's an opportunity here and it just keeps growing and killing it.
zh: 看着 Cursor 执行并在这些转变中每次领先，这是令人难以置信的，每当人们怀疑这里有机会时，它只是在继续增长并大杀四方。

speaker: Unknown
en: I mean, it's not too long ago it was like tab auto complete on it.
zh: 我的意思是，不久前它还只是标签页自动补全。

speaker: Unknown
en: And now we're in a fully cloud agents.
zh: 而现在我们处于完全的云智能体中。

speaker: Unknown
en: But just remember the time span is months.
zh: 但请记住，时间跨度只有几个月。

en: The condensed nature of this is just wild.

en: I came to the office at one point and I got a tab button and now it's just no longer even a thing.
zh: 有一次我来到办公室，我得到了一个 Tab 键，现在它甚至不再是一回事了。

zh: 是的，现在它只是可爱而已。

en: Now just talk.
zh: 现在只是谈话。

speaker: Unknown
en: Something that one of your colleagues wanted me to ask you is just what is it like to work with an exec team who truly believes recruiting is the most important thing?
zh: 你的同事想让我问你的一件事是，与一个真正相信招聘是最重要事情的高管团队一起工作是什么感觉？

speaker: Unknown
en: It's a gift and at times incredibly frustrating.
zh: 这是一种恩赐，有时也极其令人沮丧。

speaker: Unknown
en: So the gift part of it is imagine that how much they care.
zh: 所以恩赐的部分是想象一下他们有多在乎。

speaker: Unknown
en: Trying to convince a founder to go have a conversation or to do anything recruiting like, that is not a problem here.
zh: 试图说服创始人去进行对话或做任何招聘相关的事情，在这里不是问题。

speaker: Unknown
en: And we've all worked with companies where you're trying to pull them in to things.
zh: 我们都曾与这样的公司合作过，你试图把他们拉进事情里。

speaker: Unknown
en: So it's a true gift.
zh: 所以这是真正的恩赐。

speaker: Unknown
en: The challenge is they're in your shit.
zh: 挑战在于他们深入你的这些事情中。

speaker: Unknown
en: They're in it.
zh: 他们在里面。

speaker: Unknown
en: They understand it.
zh: 他们了解它。

speaker: Unknown
en: The Cursor team hired their first 80 people, roughly 80 people on their own.
zh: Cursor 团队自己雇佣了他们的前 80 个人，大约 80 个人。

speaker: Unknown
en: They know how to do it.
zh: 他们知道怎么做。

speaker: Unknown
en: They know how hard it is, which is great, but also they love it and they're in it and they want to do it.
zh: 他们知道这有多难，这很好，但他们也喜欢它，他们参与其中，并且他们想做。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so there can be zero ego about this of who has what piece and it's an all hands on deck.
zh: 所以关于谁拥有哪一部分可以有零自我，这是全员动手。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so sometimes that can be confusing on whose doing things and things that you find out about things after the fact that happened.
zh: 所以有时这可能会让人困惑，谁在做事情，以及你在事情发生后才了解到事情。

speaker: Unknown
en: But I will take that every day.
zh: 但我每天都会接受那种情况。

speaker: Unknown
en: That is extremely net positive, but there's always a counterbalance to such an advantage like that.
zh: 这是非常净正面的，但对于这样的优势总是有一个反平衡。

speaker: Unknown
en: So interesting.
zh: 太有趣了。

speaker: Unknown
en: That's like CPOs often are frustrated for that reason where the founders are always in their shit deciding.
zh: 这就像 CPO 们经常因为这个原因而感到沮丧，因为创始人总是在他们的这些事情中做决定。

speaker: Unknown
en: But they care.
zh: 但他们在乎。

speaker: Unknown
en: I'll take the effort and care with that tax any day.
zh: 我宁愿每天都要这种努力和关心以及随之而来的代价。

speaker: Unknown
en: I know one of your hot takes is that the recruiting team should be the highest paid team within the company.
zh: 我知道你的一个激进观点是，招聘团队应该是公司内部薪资最高的团队。

speaker: Adam Ward
en: And one of them. Yeah, if not. I mean, if you think about this-
zh: 其中之一。是的，如果没有。我是说，如果你考虑这个-

speaker: Unknown
en: In one of them.
zh: 其中之一。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah, if not.
zh: 是的，如果没有。

speaker: Unknown
en: I mean, if you think about this impact that they're having, and I feel like there's a supply and demand crisis around really strategic recruiters because of the somewhat transactional nature we've made recruiting over time.
zh: 我是说，如果你考虑他们正在产生的影响力，我觉得围绕真正战略级的招聘人员存在一场供需危机，因为我们随着时间的推移让招聘变得有点交易化。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so I just think there's a really small supply of recruiters who can function at this level and at this approach and style.
zh: 所以我只是认为能够在这个层面、以这种方式和风格运作的招聘人员供应非常少。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so like any other labor market, it's a cost of labor thing and there's just very few of it.
zh: 所以就像任何其他劳动力市场一样，这是一个劳动力成本的问题，而且这样的供应非常稀缺。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so we think that they have tremendous impact, but it's a really rare skillset.
zh: 所以我们认为他们拥有巨大的影响力，但这确实是一种稀缺的技能组合。

speaker: Unknown
en: Something I wanted to ask you that I forgot to ask is, we talk a lot about talent and density.
zh: 我想问你一件我忘了问的事情，我们经常谈论人才密度。

speaker: Unknown
en: How much of it is about the person specifically versus the team that you assemble around them?
zh: 这其中有多少是关于个人本身的，又有多少是关于你围绕他们组建的团队的？

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah.
zh: 是的。

speaker: Unknown
en: I feel like where companies overly focus is an individual, and unless they are a team of one, it's actually, if you think about amazing leadership and amazing managers, they're actually quite great puzzle builders.
zh: 我觉得公司过度关注的地方在于个人，除非他们是光杆司令团队，其实，如果你想想出色的领导和出色的管理者，他们实际上是非常棒的拼图构建者。

speaker: Unknown
en: And they think about building these teams that are complimentary together and then help them excel.
zh: 他们考虑建立互补的团队，然后帮助团队蓬勃发展。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so talent density is not a single piece, unless the numerator and denominator are both one.
zh: 所以人才密度不是单一的一块，除非分子和分母都是一。

speaker: Unknown
en: But that's not the case.
zh: 但事实并非如此。

speaker: Unknown
en: Often this is one over how many people.
zh: 通常这是一个人除以多少人。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so talent density is actually a collective nature of individuals and humans.
zh: 所以人才密度实际上是个体和人类的集体性质。

speaker: Unknown
en: But we often, because you are recruiting one human at a time, I think sometimes we get overly focused on that specific 10Xer thing.
zh: 但我们经常因为一次只招募一个人，我认为有时我们过度关注那个特定的 10Xer（10倍人才）。

speaker: Unknown
en: And actually, I like to think a little bit more around exponential around 10X of a team versus an individual.
zh: 其实，我更喜欢围绕团队的 10X（10倍）而不是个人的 10X 来考虑指数级增长。

speaker: Unknown
en: I don't think you can have a 10X person on a bad team.
zh: 我认为你不可能在一个糟糕的团队里拥有一个 10X（10倍效能）的人。

speaker: Unknown
en: It just doesn't exist.
zh: 这是不存在的。

speaker: Unknown
en: I used to think when we were at my last company, we can't be a great service provider if we don't have a great client.
zh: 我以前认为当我们在我上一家公司时，如果我们没有很棒的客户，我们就无法成为很棒的服务提供商。

speaker: Unknown
en: There's just a bar there.
zh: 那里是有门槛的。

speaker: Unknown
en: And similarly, a person that might be excellent is going to be throttled if they're not on a strong and supportive team.
zh: 同样，一个可能很优秀的人，如果他们不在一个强大和支持性的团队中，就会被限制发挥。

speaker: Unknown
en: That makes sense to me.
zh: 这对我来说有道理。

speaker: Unknown
en: Okay.
zh: 好的。

speaker: Unknown
en: I'm going to ask you a bunch of random questions.
zh: 我要问你一堆随机的问题。

speaker: Unknown
en: Okay.
zh: 好的。

speaker: Unknown
en: Again, I think people are going to be hearing this and be like, "I need Adam immediately.
zh: 同样，我认为人们听到这个后会想，“我马上需要 Adam。

speaker: Unknown
en: We need help."
zh: 我们需要帮助。”

speaker: Unknown
en: And they're not going to be able to get that, because you've got a job.
zh: 而且他们没法得到那个，因为你有一份工作。

speaker: Unknown
en: So I'm going to try to extract as much as I can while we're here.
zh: 所以我要在我们在一起的时候尽可能多地挖掘信息。

speaker: Unknown
en: One is, say you're an early stage company thinking about hiring, setting up your hiring approach, what's the most common ways that early stage companies and founders f-up their early team in hiring?
zh: 一个是，假设你是一家早期公司，正在考虑招聘，建立你的招聘方法，早期公司和创始人在早期团队招聘中搞砸的最常见方式是什么？

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah.
zh: 是的。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think the thing they try to do is do this silver bullet hire, which is a first head of talent, and they collapse two competing skill sets into one.
zh: 我认为他们试图做的是这种银弹式招聘，也就是第一位人才主管，他们把两种相互竞争的技能组合并到了一个人身上。

speaker: Unknown
en: Okay.
zh: 好的。

speaker: Unknown
en: So generally, as a founder, when you're ready to hire your first recruiter, you're probably behind on hiring.
zh: 所以通常，作为创始人，当你准备好雇佣你的第一位招聘人员时，你可能在招聘进度上落后了。

speaker: Unknown
en: There's a problem to solve there, you're behind on hiring.
zh: 那里有一个要解决的问题，你在招聘进度上落后了。

speaker: Unknown
en: So maybe there's a debt of roles to fill, five, 10, 15.
zh: 所以可能有一些未填补的职位债务，5个，10个，15个。

speaker: Unknown
en: But you also are hiring someone at this stage because you want them to build a system.
zh: 但你在这一阶段雇佣某人也是因为你希望他们建立一个系统。

speaker: Unknown
en: They might be like, "Wow, I want to build something like Adam's talking about."
zh: 他们可能会想，“哇，我想建立像 Adam 说的那样的东西。”

speaker: Unknown
en: So you're trying to build this, hire someone who can also put in the right pieces to help scale out.
zh: 所以你试图建立这个，雇佣一个能够安放合适组件来帮助规模化的人。

speaker: Unknown
en: And those are competing interests, because a person wants to come in and like just any new hire, they want to prove out, they want to make hires, but they might not put in the system.
zh: 而这些是相互冲突的利益，因为一个人想进来，就像任何新员工一样，他们想证明自己，他们想招到人，但他们可能不会建立系统。

speaker: Unknown
en: Or they might put in the system, but not make any hires, and now you're not [inaudible 01:12:41].
zh: 或者他们可能建立了系统，但没有招到任何人，现在你就不是[听不清 01:12:41]。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so they try to collapse this into one role, and generally that's a mistake.
zh: 所以他们试图将这两者合并到一个角色中，通常这是一个错误。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so we recommend decoupling those things.
zh: 所以我们建议将这些事情解耦。

speaker: Unknown
en: So that means you still might hire one person, but can you get some help with the other one?
zh: 这意味着你可能仍然雇佣一个人，但你能在另一方面获得一些帮助吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: I'm going to hire the person who's going to put in the right system, but I'm going to partner them with a contingent recruiter or something else to make some short-term progress while they're in to teach the company how to do this through these roles that they feel that they're helping orchestrate, or vice versa, I might bring in someone to help us put in the right foundation, which we did at GBD.
zh: 我要雇佣那个会安放合适系统的人，但我会让他们与一位按结果付费的招聘人员或其他东西合作，以便在他们入职期间通过他们觉得帮助协调的角色，通过教公司如何做这些事情来取得短期进展，反之亦然，我可以请人来帮助我们安放正确的基础，我们在 GBD 就这么做了。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then they could hire a really high-powered IC recruiter who can execute.
zh: 然后他们可以雇佣一位真正高能的 IC（个人贡献者）招聘人员来执行。

speaker: Unknown
en: Amazing.
zh: 太棒了。

speaker: Unknown
en: That makes all the sense in the world.
zh: 这完全有道理。

speaker: Unknown
en: When you're looking for that first recruiting hire, is there anything else you think is important to look for?
zh: 当你在寻找第一位招聘人员时，还有其他你认为重要的因素需要考虑吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: I know it depends on maybe which of these two buckets they're going to be in, but any other advice?
zh: 我知道这可能取决于他们将属于这两类中的哪一类，但还有其他建议吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah.
zh: 是的。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think number one is that they are curious and business focused.
zh: 我认为第一点是，他们要有好奇心且以业务为导向。

speaker: Unknown
en: They're an early member of the team.
zh: 他们是团队的早期成员。

speaker: Unknown
en: They got to be really curious understanding of how the business works and how each of those hires is going to change the slope of the business.
zh: 他们必须非常有好奇心，去理解业务是如何运作的，以及每一次招聘将如何改变业务的斜率。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so often that means that they have all these interesting...
zh: 所以通常这意味着他们拥有所有这些有趣的……

speaker: Unknown
en: It shows up in lots of way, curious people.
zh: 这种好奇心以很多种方式表现出来，好奇的人。

speaker: Unknown
en: But I think that's the number one thing I think of.
zh: 但我认为这是我想到的第一件事。

speaker: Unknown
en: The number two one, and I think these sometimes get switched, is just high motor.
zh: 第二点，我认为有时候这两点会互换，就是要有极高的动力。

speaker: Unknown
en: Someone who understands the grind that it will be and the pace that it works and is down for it.
zh: 一个能理解这种苦差子、这种工作节奏，并且乐在其中的人。

speaker: Unknown
en: And that doesn't mean they have to be younger, or it doesn't mean anything.
zh: 这并不意味着他们必须更年轻，或者不意味着任何事情。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's just that they love working at this edge of overwhelmedness.
zh: 只是他们喜欢这种处于压倒性边缘的工作状态。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so I often think about my team as we want the water level to be right here, and so you're breathing.
zh: 所以我经常思考我的团队，就像我们要把水位设在这里，这样你可以呼吸。

speaker: Unknown
en: And if you've met any recruiters, recruiters are excellent at 90 to 110% capacity, and are terrible outside of that.
zh: 如果你见过任何招聘人员，招聘人员在 90% 到 110% 的容量时表现出色，而在这个范围之外就很糟糕。

speaker: Unknown
en: If they only have half a rec load, they are useless, or if they're way overwhelmed, also just overwhelmed.
zh: 如果他们只有一半的招聘负荷，他们就没用，或者如果他们不堪重负，也会不知所措。

speaker: Unknown
en: But they're great at this middle ground of edge of adrenaline rush busy, and you want to find those people.
zh: 但他们擅长这种处于肾上腺素激增忙碌状态的中间地带，你想找到这些人。

speaker: Unknown
en: Oh, man.
zh: 天哪。

speaker: Unknown
en: So along those lines, I've heard from a bunch of people that you just have a huge followship on your team.
zh: 所以顺着这个思路，我从很多人那里听说，你在团队中拥有巨大的追随者。

speaker: Unknown
en: There's a lot of heads of talent from other companies that decided to join your team to be ICs.
zh: 有很多来自其他公司的人才负责人决定加入你的团队担任独立贡献者。

speaker: Unknown
en: What are some things you've learned about building incredible teams, keeping people working for you over the long term?
zh: 关于建立令人难以置信的团队、让人们长期为你工作，你学到了什么？

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah.
zh: 是的。

speaker: Unknown
en: One thing I learned is, at each place my team has looked different, because the company, how they think about recruiting or the product is different.
zh: 我学到的一件事是，在每个地方，我的团队看起来都不一样，因为公司、他们对招聘的看法或产品是不同的。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so the Cursor way demanded a different type of team.
zh: 所以 Cursor 的方式需要一种不同类型的团队。

speaker: Unknown
en: It demanded this level of recruiter and who understands the leadership recruiting motion, who's not going to get caught up in the numbers game of the funnel do.
zh: 它需要这种级别的招聘人员，能够理解领导层招聘运作模式，不会陷入漏斗数据的数字游戏中。

speaker: Unknown
en: They have this confidence and they have a network that they can tap into.
zh: 他们有这种自信，并且拥有可以利用的人脉网络。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so I think we talked a lot about hiring managers, other people networks, but seasoned great recruiters have their own networks too.
zh: 所以我想我们谈论了很多关于招聘经理、其他人的网络，但经验丰富的优秀招聘人员也有自己的网络。
